name: Zimakani
confidence_why: The only description of Zimakani stress is one hedged sentence in Voorhoeve 1975, drawn from his own 1969 Lake Murray survey, that stress "seems to be non-phonemic" with no placement given, while his fuller survey report (Voorhoeve 1970) and every other available source say nothing about stress, and no grammar or phonology of the language exists.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only published statement is negative: stress is (tentatively) not phonemic, i.e. not contrastive, and by extension from the Boazi statement the language is non-tonal. No placement rule (initial/final/weight) is given anywhere; the reading 'no word stress according to the source' is used here in the sense 'no contrastive word stress reported', not a claim that words lack prominence. The 1970 survey, on which the 1975 chapter draws, is silent on stress and its phonetic wordlist carries no stress marks.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the statement is hedged ('seems to be') and rests on three weeks of survey fieldwork in March 1969 (Voorhoeve 1970: 4).
new_statements.domain_note: Survey-level phoneme inventory statement; no distinction of word vs phrase or citation forms. Applies to the Zimakani dialect data (Voorhoeve 1970 says Begua 'seems to have an identical sound system').
new_statements.identity_note: Voorhoeve's 1975 statement is under the heading 'Zimakani' (language, both dialects Zimakani and Begua = zima1244); his 1970 survey says Begua 'seems to have an identical sound system'. The parallel Boazi statement on p. 356 refers to the sister language Kuni-Boazi (Boset/South Boazi dialect, ISO kvg), not to Zimakani. Ethnologue/Glottolog alternate names: Dea, Village Z, Babwa/Baegwa/Bagwa, Begua.

sources.note: Section 2 'Phonology' pp. 4-6 gives consonant and vowel phonemes of Boset-Boazi and the differences in North Boazi, Kuini, Zimakani (2.5, p. 6) and Begua; section 2.6 on clusters and final consonants. Nothing on stress, accent or tone; the 242-item comparative wordlist (pp. 7-14, phonetic notation) carries no stress marks. (The 'Stress rules' hits in this volume belong to Blowers & Blowers' Kaugel paper, pp. 40-45.)
